questions.q: What is the common spacing for vertical rebars in a standard 150mm CHB wall?
o: 0.60 meters to 0.80 meters (depending on structural specs).
questions.n: Standard practice typically places vertical bars at 400mm, 600mm, or 800mm centers depending on the height and purpose of the wall.

questions.q: What is the standard horizontal rebar spacing for CHB walls?
o: Every 2 to 3 layers of blocks (0.40m to 0.60m).
At the bottom and top layers only
Every 4 to 5 layers of blocks (0.80m to 1.00m)
questions.n: Standard Philippine construction typically requires horizontal reinforcement at every second or third course of blocks.

questions.q: What happens to wood when it loses moisture in a dry environment?
questions.n: As wood cells lose bound water, they contract, causing the overall volume of the timber to decrease.

questions.q: What happens to wood when it absorbs moisture in a humid environment?
questions.n: Wood is hygroscopic; absorbing moisture from the air causes the wood fibers to swell and the material to grow in dimension.

questions.q: In electrical systems, what is the purpose of a "Three-way switch"?
o: To control a single light fixture from three or more locations
To control a single light fixture from two different locations.
To provide three different levels of brightness
To control three different lights from one location
questions.n: Three-way switches are used in pairs to allow a light (like in a hallway or stairs) to be toggled from two separate points.

questions.q: What is the standard mounting height for a light switch from the finished floor line?
questions.n: This range places the switch at a comfortable reaching height for the average adult standing up.

questions.q: What is the standard mounting height for a convenience outlet (CO) in a general living area?
questions.n: 300mm (or 12 inches) is the standard height for outlets in living rooms and bedrooms, keeping cords relatively hidden.

questions.q: What is a "P-trap" used for?
o: To increase water pressure in the fixture
To provide a water seal that prevents sewer gases from entering the building.
To connect horizontal and vertical pipes
questions.n: The curved shape holds a small amount of water (seal) that prevents methane and other odors from traveling up the pipe.

questions.q: What is the minimum slope for a horizontal drainage pipe to ensure proper flow?
questions.n: A 2% slope provides enough velocity to transport solids without the water flowing too fast and leaving solids behind.

questions.q: What is the term for the pipe that connects the building drain to the public sewer?
questions.n: The building sewer is the extension from the building drain to the public sewer system or other point of disposal.

questions.q: What is the standard size of a Concrete Hollow Block (CHB) in the Philippines?
questions.n: Regardless of thickness, the face of a standard block is always 200mm high and 400mm long.

questions.q: What are the common thicknesses of CHB used for exterior walls?
questions.n: Exterior walls typically use 6-inch blocks to provide better structural stability and space for reinforcement.

questions.q: What is the common thickness of CHB used for interior partitions?
questions.n: The 4-inch block is the standard for interior walls to maximize usable floor space while providing adequate privacy.

questions.q: What is the term for a beam that supports the load of a wall above an opening, like a door or window?
questions.n: A lintel is a horizontal structural member that spans the top of an opening and carries the weight of the masonry above.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a "Stiffener Column"?
o: To provide lateral stability to long stretches of CHB walls.
To act as a decorative element
questions.n: Stiffeners (usually every 3 meters) break up the length of a wall to prevent it from buckling or toppling under lateral loads.

questions.q: What do you call the temporary timber or steel structure used to support a concrete slab while it is curing?
questions.n: Formwork shapes the concrete, while shoring (the vertical supports) keeps it in place until it can support its own weight.

questions.q: What is "Curing" in concrete work?
o: Maintaining moisture and temperature conditions to allow concrete to develop its full strength.
The process of mixing cement and water
Adding chemicals to make concrete dry faster
The chemical reaction that turns cement into rock
questions.n: Proper curing prevents the water needed for hydration from evaporating too quickly.

questions.q: What is the standard curing period for ordinary Portland cement concrete to reach most of its strength?
questions.n: Design strength (f'c) is legally and structurally measured at the 28-day mark.

questions.q: What is the term for the process of leveling and smoothing the top surface of a freshly poured concrete slab?
questions.n: Screeding uses a straight edge pulled across the forms to level the concrete to the correct elevation.

questions.q: What is a "Power Trowel" used for?
o: To vibrate concrete to remove air bubbles
To create a very smooth, dense finish on large concrete floor areas.
To mix concrete in large quantities
questions.n: Also known as a 'helicopter,' it uses rotating blades to burnish the surface of a slab.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a "Cleanout" in a plumbing system?
o: To provide access for clearing clogs in the drainage pipes.
To drain the system during repairs
To allow air into the pipes
questions.n: Cleanouts are capped openings located at intervals to allow plumbing snakes to reach blockages.

questions.q: What does a "Circuit Breaker" do in an electrical panel?
o: It automatically shuts off power when it detects an overload or short circuit.
It converts AC to DC power
It measures how much electricity is being used
questions.n: It is a safety device designed to protect the wiring from damage caused by excess current.

questions.q: In smart buildings, what does "Occupancy Sensing" control?
o: Lighting and HVAC based on whether people are in the room.
Who is allowed to enter the building
The weight limits of the elevator
questions.n: It saves energy by turning off systems in unoccupied areas.

questions.q: What is the main component of Fiber Optic cables?
questions.n: Fiber optics use very thin strands of glass or plastic to transmit data as pulses of light.

questions.q: What is "Daylight Harvesting"?
o: A smart building strategy that dims electric lights when natural sunlight is sufficient.
questions.n: It uses photosensors to adjust interior lighting levels based on the amount of available natural light.

questions.q: What is a "Mullion"?
o: A decorative trim around a door
A vertical member that separates window units or glass panes.
A horizontal member between door panels
The frame that holds the glass
questions.n: Mullions provide structural support to the window assembly.

questions.q: What is a "Transom"?
o: A vertical divider in a window
A structural beam in the roof
A horizontal member above a door or window that separates it from a window above.
questions.n: Transoms often allow for 'transom windows' to be placed above a door for light and air.

questions.q: What is the term for a door that is hinged on one side and opens like a book?
questions.n: The most common door type, which pivots on hinges along one vertical edge.

questions.q: What is a "Pocket Door"?
o: A door that only opens halfway
A very small door for pets
A door with many storage pockets
A sliding door that disappears into a compartment in the adjacent wall.
questions.n: It is perfect for saving floor space because it doesn't require a swing radius or wall space for an open leaf.

questions.q: What is the standard height of a kitchen counter?
questions.n: This range is ergonomic for food preparation for the average adult.

questions.q: What is the standard depth of a kitchen base cabinet?
questions.n: 600mm is the industry standard depth to accommodate sinks, cooktops, and appliances.

questions.q: What is the term for a small, elevated window usually used for ventilation in bathrooms?
questions.n: Clerestory windows are high in the wall to provide light and air while maintaining privacy.

questions.q: What is the purpose of an "Expansion Joint" in long buildings?
o: To make the building look longer
To allow the building to expand and contract due to thermal changes without cracking.
To allow for future building additions
To provide a location for electrical wires
questions.n: Long structures can crack if they aren't allowed to move slightly as they heat up and cool down.

questions.q: What do you call the decorative molding at the junction of a wall and a ceiling?
questions.n: Cornices provide a finished transition between the vertical and horizontal planes of a room.

questions.q: What do you call the protective molding at the junction of a wall and a floor?
questions.n: It protects the wall from kicks and cleaning equipment while covering the joint between floor and wall.

questions.q: What is the primary use of "Vapor Barrier" in construction?
o: To keep the building warm in winter
To prevent moisture from the ground or air from seeping into the building envelope.
questions.n: Vapor barriers (like poly sheeting) prevent condensation and dampness inside walls and floors.

questions.q: What is the standard width of a residential hallway?
questions.n: 1.00m is the preferred standard for comfortable circulation, though 0.90m is often the code minimum.

questions.q: What is the "Rough-in" stage of construction?
o: Installing the internal components (pipes, wires, ducts) before the walls are closed.
Moving the furniture into the building
Applying the final coat of paint
questions.n: Roughing-in allows for the backbone of the utilities to be inspected before they are hidden by drywalls or plaster.

questions.q: What is the purpose of "Gravel Bed" under a ground floor slab?
o: To provide a stable base and prevent capillary action (moisture rising).
To make the floor more comfortable to walk on
To provide a home for beneficial insects
questions.n: The air gaps between the stones break the surface tension that would otherwise pull water up from the soil into the slab.

questions.q: What is a "Slab on Fill"?
o: A concrete slab that rests directly on compacted soil or gravel.
A slab used for filling holes in the wall
A decorative slab on top of a table
A slab that hangs from the roof
questions.n: It 'fills' the area within the foundation walls and is supported by the ground rather than just by beams.

questions.q: What is the term for the structural framework of a roof?
questions.n: A truss is a framework of members (usually triangles) that forms a rigid structure to support the roof.

questions.q: What is the horizontal member that supports the common rafters or roofing sheets?
questions.n: Purlins run perpendicular to the rafters (or trusses) to provide a base for the roofing material.

questions.q: What is the highest point of a pitched roof?
questions.n: The ridge is the horizontal line at the junction of the highest edges of two sloping roof surfaces.

questions.q: What is a "Fascia Board"?
o: The vertical board attached to the ends of the rafters where the gutter is usually mounted.
The material used to insulate the roof
A structural column inside the house
questions.n: It provides a finished edge to the roofline and a sturdy surface for gutters.

questions.q: What is the purpose of "Scaffolding"?
o: To provide permanent support for the roof
To store large amounts of soil
A temporary structure to support workers and materials during construction or repair.
To keep the building cool during construction
questions.n: Scaffolding allows workers to safely access high areas of a building.

questions.q: What is "Ductile Detailing"?
o: Providing reinforcement in a way that allows the structure to bend without breaking during seismic events.
Adding more windows to a building
questions.n: Ductility is essential in earthquake zones to prevent brittle failure and total collapse.

questions.q: In a smart home, what is a "Hub"?
o: The central device that connects and controls all smart devices in the network.
The place where you store your tools
questions.n: The hub acts as the brain that translates different signals (Zigbee, Z-Wave, etc.) so devices can work together.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of an LED light over an incandescent bulb?
o: It is cheaper to buy initially
Higher energy efficiency and longer lifespan.
questions.n: LEDs use significantly less power and can last 25,000 hours or more compared to 1,000 hours for incandescent bulbs.

questions.q: What is a "Sump Pump" used for?
o: To provide high-pressure water for showers
To pump water to the roof tank
To remove water that has accumulated in a water-collecting sump pit, commonly found in basements.
questions.n: It prevents flooding by pumping out groundwater or runoff that collects in low points.

questions.q: What is the most important mindset for an examinee during a difficult Building Technology exam?
o: To finish as fast as possible to go home
To give up if the first five questions are too hard
To stay calm, take deep breaths, and analyze the questions logically based on site experience.
To memorize all the numbers without understanding them
questions.n: Many Building Tech questions can be solved by visualizing real construction site scenarios and logical material behavior.
